title: Building a place for clean-energy research to move
excerpt: Why I joined Plaksha Clean Energy Forum’s founding team: to help more students find real energy questions, work with mentors and industry, and turn research into useful projects.
html:
A field note · Plaksha Clean Energy Forum

Building a place for clean-energy ideas to move.

I am part of the founding team helping build a student-facing community for clean-energy research, real problems and people ready to work on them.

Explore Plaksha CEF ↗

Why this matters to meClean energy is one of the defining areas to build in. India needs more research, more ways into the work, and more people building together.

Energy is woven into ordinary life: the rooms we cool, the journeys we make, the things we produce and the services we rely on. The choices behind it shape affordability, resilience, access and the air around us. These are not distant questions for India. They are practical questions already shaping our future.

I joined the founding team of Plaksha Clean Energy Forum because I want more students to get close to those questions early: to find a problem, learn how to investigate it, meet people working in the field and see where their contribution could lead.

A forum built around doing

Plaksha CEF is a growing community at Plaksha University under the Indorama Ventures Center for Clean Energy. Its aim is to connect research, real-world problems and people willing to explore solutions. The work is still at an early stage, which makes this a moment to shape how it grows.

01 / FINDStart with a real questionListen to problems from research, industry and communities.
02 / SHAPEMake a project of itTurn a broad challenge into a clear scope and useful next step.
03 / CONNECTBring people togetherHelp students meet faculty, mentors and industry practitioners.
04 / LEARNShare what the work teachesDocument progress, improve the approach and make learning travel.

My part in the beginning

My role is Research & Entrepreneurship Head. I sit between questions worth pursuing, the projects that could make them concrete, and the people who might help them grow. I want the forum to make room for rigorous research and practical experimentation, while helping students understand how ideas meet real constraints.

My own work with clean-energy research at Plaksha has made that connection clearer to me. A technical idea becomes useful through people, behaviour, deployment and context. Students should have more opportunities to take part in that full journey, not only read about it from a distance.

What I hope we can build: accessible ways for students to begin meaningful work, deeper projects shaped around real questions, and stronger links between students, mentors, researchers and industry.

Still at the start

We are early. The forum is a community effort within a much larger energy challenge, and its first projects are a chance to learn what structure, support and collaboration are actually useful. I do not want to describe a future ambition as an existing outcome. I want us to earn it through the work.

I hope Plaksha CEF grows into a place where a student can arrive curious, find a problem worth staying with, and meet collaborators who help turn that curiosity into research, a project or something useful beyond campus. If you are a student, mentor, researcher or industry practitioner interested in clean energy, I would love for you to explore it with us.
